_meta.content: For each scenario (6) and question (6), in page order: found (quoted results of NASA's experiments), criteria, process, recorded, unprocessed, no_record, caveats; and a headline built from counts only.
_meta.shared_dictionaries: To keep the file small, the text, quote, conditions and printed values of a finding are held once in 'findings' (key: finding_id) and the text, quote, place and printed values of an item once in 'items' (key: item_id); documents are in 'documents' (key: document_id). Entries of the blocks refer to them by id and carry their source (item id, document title, version, where, url, access).

order_rule.text: Results are ranked by the conditions their own words state, against the ranges of the environment, with no weights and no assumed values: first the results that state an oxygen and a pressure inside the ranges of the environment; then those that state at least one of its conditions (oxygen, pressure, gravity level) inside its range and none outside; then those that state no oxygen, pressure or gravity level; last those listed for this environment under other conditions. Inside a group: a result whose item is labelled measured (or carries no label) comes before a result labelled computed by the authors, simulation or preliminary (field result_kind of the item, see result_kind); then a result that names a material comes first; then by item id; then in the order of findings.csv. The groups are those of findings_by_environment.json; this file does not place a result again.

groups.label: At the oxygen and pressure of this environment
About one stated condition of this environment
Stated without oxygen, pressure or gravity level
At other stated conditions (not listed for this environment by findings_by_environment.json)

result_kind.note: Field 'result_kind' of a reference item (added 2026-11-15; items added earlier carry none and are ordered as measured). An item whose kind is not measured begins its text with the label of its kind; check U5 verifies it. 'relation' is set for an item whose experiment is not a PSI investigation of this catalogue; such an item has 'investigation' null.

labels.computed_by_authors: Computed by the authors, not a measurement:

_meta.printed_values: Printed values are the numbers of the item exactly as held in references.json, each with the column or quantity it was printed under. The team computes nothing with them.

values_rules.rows: A 'rows' list: one printed value per field of a row that is not a row label ('row_label_fields'); the row labels are kept with each value.
values_rules.matrix: An object with one 'columns_*' list and lists of the same length under other keys: one printed value per key and column; the key is the material as printed, the column is printed with its own unit.
values_rules.list: A list under a key that ends in '_range' is one printed value (the range as held); any other list gives one printed value per element.
values_rules.object: An object of plain values: one printed value per key.
values_rules.scalar: A number or a text: one printed value.
values_rules.entry_rows: An entry made from one row of a table (row_source 'rows[i]') takes the values of that row; an entry made from one column of a table (column_of) takes that column; an entry made from element i of a list (row_source 'key[i]') takes element i of that list and of every other top-level list of the item with the same length. An entry with a row but neither takes no printed value ('values_scope' not_split_by_row): the item's values stay in 'items'. An entry without a row takes all values of the item.

_meta.units: The unit of a printed value is taken from the item's 'values' field 'unit' where it has one; otherwise from the key of the value by the first rule below whose token is in the key (the keys are the team's names for the printed columns; the unit is the unit those names carry). A key that matches no rule has no unit. The rules from flow_cms to he_pct at the head of the list were added on 2026-11-15 for the keys of the items added that day; they leave the unit of every value held before unchanged.

access_values.full_text_read: the cited passage was read in the document
access_values.abstract_only: only the public abstract or catalogue page was read
access_values.cited_not_read: known only through a citation in another listed document
access_values.read_by_teammate: the passage was read in the document by another session of the team, which reported the wording; not read by the session that wrote this file

_meta.not_research_guidance: A research exploration tool, not safety guidance. Read by an AI agent; not checked by a person.
_meta.team_output: Groups, order, headlines and counts are the team's computation from the files named in 'inputs'; they are not NASA's conclusions.

6001B.OI.def.text: Oxygen index: the minimum concentration of oxygen (volume percent) in an oxygen-nitrogen mixture that will just support flaming combustion of a material initially at room temperature under the conditions of ASTM D2863.
6001B.OI.def.quote: Oxygen index: The minimum concentration of oxygen, expressed as a volume percent, in a mixture of oxygen and nitrogen that will just support flaming combustion of a material initially at room temperature under the conditions of ASTM D2863
6001B.OI.def.item_note: Does not state the pressure of the oxygen-index test; it delegates the conditions to ASTM D2863 (not read in full).

6001B.T1.ambient.text: Ambient conditions: 20.9 percent oxygen, 101.4 kPa (14.7 psia), 23 +/-5 degC.

6001B.T1.atmosphere.text: Test 1 evaluates the material in the worst-case atmosphere to which it could be exposed; the oxygen level is the highest the material could witness in use.

6001B.T1.failenv.text: Failure of any one specimen constitutes failure of the material in that test environment.
6001B.T1.failenv.quote: Failure of any one specimen constitutes failure of the material in that test environment.
6001B.T1.failenv.item_note: Speaks of failure only; it does not say that a pass is limited to that environment (ICES-2014-179 says that, see C02).

6001B.T1.focr59.text: Test 1 shall evaluate the candidate material in the worst-case atmosphere to which the material could be exposed.
6001B.T1.focr59.quote: Test 1 shall evaluate the candidate material in the worst-case atmosphere to which the material could be exposed.
6001B.T1.focr59.item_note: Does not define 'atmosphere' in this sentence and gives no number. It does not say the result holds in any other atmosphere.

6001B.T1.moc.text: Maximum Oxygen Concentration (MOC): the maximum oxygen concentration at which at least five specimens pass the acceptance criteria of Test 1.
6001B.T1.moc.quote: Maximum Oxygen Concentration: The maximum oxygen concentration at which at least five specimens pass the acceptance criteria of this test.

6001B.T1.noflow.text: Air shall not be allowed to flow during tests.
6001B.T1.noflow.quote: Air shall not be allowed to flow during tests.
6001B.T1.noflow.item_note: The standard states no velocity; buoyant flow is present in normal gravity.

6001B.T1.o2level.text: The Test 1 atmosphere is a mixture of gaseous oxygen and nitrogen with the oxygen level the highest the material could witness in use conditions.
6001B.T1.o2level.quote: The test atmosphere shall consist of a mixture of GOX and GN2, with the oxygen level being the highest that the material could witness in use conditions.
6001B.T1.o2level.item_note: Says nothing about the pressure of the test. Pressure enters Test 1 only through 'worst-case atmosphere' (7.1.2a) and the general definition (3.2, 4.1f).

6001B.T1.pass.text: A material is self-extinguishing if no specimen burns more than 15 cm and no specimen propagates a flame by transfer of burning debris.

6001B.T1.purpose.text: Test 1 determines whether a material, when exposed to a standard ignition source, will self-extinguish and not transfer burning debris that can ignite adjacent materials.
6001B.T1.purpose.quote: The purpose of this test is to determine if a material, when exposed to a standard ignition source, will self-extinguish and not transfer burning debris, which can ignite adjacent materials.

6001B.def.worstcase.text: Worst-case anticipated use environment: the most hazardous pressure, temperature, material thickness and/or fluid exposure conditions.

6001B.def.worstcase.item_note: The definition lists pressure, temperature, thickness and fluid exposure; it does not list oxygen concentration (that is added for Test 1 in 7.1.4f). It does not say which pressure is 'most hazardous'.

6001B.focr12.text: The worst-case anticipated use environment (most hazardous pressure, temperature, material thickness and fluid exposure conditions) shall be used in the evaluation of material suitability.
6001B.focr12.quote: The worst-case anticipated use environment (most hazardous pressure, temperature, material thickness, and fluid exposure conditions) shall be used in the evaluation of material suitability.
6001B.focr12.item_note: A requirement on material evaluation, not a definition of a flammability limit.

EAWG.testing.text: A white paper appended to the report (Appendix E-2) states that the lander and habitat recommendations require materials ignition and flammability testing and certification to 34% oxygen. The Executive Summary recommends a modified standard NASA flammability test to generate ignition threshold data, and says lander materials need flammability testing at a maximum oxygen concentration outside the existing shuttle/ISS database.
EAWG.testing.quote: These recommendations will also require materials ignition and flammability testing and certification to 34% oxygen concentration.
EAWG.testing.tagging_note: 'testing and certification to 34% oxygen' is a certification level (values key o2_pct_max); it is normalized as the value 34.

EAWG.ignthreshold.text: Verbatim wording for the existing item EAWG.testing: the ignition threshold data come from a modified standard flammability test and serve to identify materials at risk from increases in oxygen concentration. The report does not say that the threshold is an ignition energy or an ignition time.
EAWG.ignthreshold.quote: Constellation should institute a modified standard NASA flammability test to generate ignition threshold data for key spacecraft materials. This modified test will allow NASA to identify materials at risk from increases in oxygen concentration

CH.hardware.text: CFI-G burner streams reached up to 85% oxygen.

oxygen: burner streams reached up to 85% oxygen

CH.hardware.tagging_note: 85% is the oxygen of a burner stream, not of an atmosphere; it is kept as words.

TB14639.worstcase.text: Test 1 is conducted in the most severe environment expected in the spacecraft, currently 30% oxygen at 10.2 psia.

TB14639.modified.text: A modified Test 1 measures the actual upward flammability limit (akin to the Limiting Oxygen Index) so that the margin of safety in the use environment can be assessed.

ICES19.boundary.text: The flammability boundary is expressed in oxygen concentration and flow velocity, with a quenching branch at low flow and a blowoff branch at high flow.

ICES19.limits.text: BASS-II PMMA: minimum oxygen concentration in the flammability boundary from the concurrent (stagnation-flow) rod tests 13.6% O2; minimum flammable value for the opposed-flow rods 16.3% O2 (no comparable boundary was obtained for opposed flow); normal-gravity PMMA extinction limits 17% O2 (downward spread) and 15.4% O2 (upward spread).
ICES19.limits.tagging_note: The oxygen numbers (13.6, 16.3, 17 and 15.4% O2) are reported limits, not the atmosphere of a test, and are not normalized. 'normal-gravity' is written for two of the four limits; the item does not state the gravity level of the two BASS-II limits, so no gravity level is normalized.

ICES19.fanoff.text: In BASS-II the flames always quenched when the fan was turned off. The authors call turning off ventilation an excellent mitigation strategy for the ISS, and add that earlier quiescent tests at elevated oxygen suggest ventilation may not be necessary for a flame to survive in high-oxygen low-pressure atmospheres or in partial gravity, so the strategy may not be applicable in future exploration missions.
ICES19.fanoff.quote: so this mitigation strategy may not be applicable in future exploration missions

oxygen: earlier quiescent tests at elevated oxygen
flow: when the fan was turned off

ICES19.fanoff.tagging_note: The item holds a result (the flames quenched when the fan was turned off) and a caveat (the strategy may not be applicable in future exploration missions); kind is set to result. 'high-oxygen low-pressure atmospheres' and 'partial gravity' are named for the caveat only and without a number; they are kept as words.

ICES19.pressure.text: BASS-II varied oxygen from 13% to 22% by nitrogen dilution of the ISS atmosphere in the glovebox working volume; pressure was not varied from 1 atmosphere.
ICES19.pressure.quote: Pressure was not varied from 1 atmosphere.
ICES19.pressure.tagging_note: Oxygen is a range varied over the investigation, not the oxygen of one test.

ICES19.sensors.text: On-board sensors measured the initial and final oxygen concentrations, to determine oxygen depletion and extinction oxygen concentrations, and the completeness of combustion (CO, CO2 sensor).
ICES19.sensors.quote: to determine oxygen depletion, extinction oxygen concentrations, and the completeness of combustion (CO, CO2 sensor)
ICES19.sensors.tagging_note: States what the sensors measured and for what purpose; it reports no value.

ICES19.coratio.text: The range of the CO/CO2 molar ratio produced in the microgravity flames is 0.01 to 0.1.
ICES19.coratio.quote: The range of the CO/CO2 molar ratio produced in microgravity flames is 0.01-0.1

ICES19.test1conditions.text: A flame spread of more than 15 cm in NASA Test 1 makes the material count as flammable at the oxygen and pressure of that test.
ICES19.test1conditions.quote: If the flame spreads more than 15 cm in NASA Test 1, the material is considered flammable under the oxygen and pressure conditions

ICES19.lowpressure.text: Turning off the ventilation, the current ISS practice, may fail to put out a flame for some materials planned for future exploration missions in high oxygen, lower pressure atmospheres.
ICES19.lowpressure.quote: deactivating the ventilation, as is currently done on the ISS, may not be sufficient to extinguish a flame in high oxygen lower pressure atmospheres

OF2012.margin.text: Oxygen margins of safety (low-gravity limit minus 1g limit, % O2 by mole) were negative by as much as -5.75 (lunar gravity, Mylar G at 10.2 psia); the largest at Martian gravity was -3.35 (Nomex HT90-40) and at 0g -4.1 (Mylar G). Normal-gravity screening tests may not be conservative. The low-g limits come from 5 s drop tests and their extinction criteria are not the same as in 1g.
OF2012.margin.tagging_note: '10.2 psia' is written for one of the three margins (lunar gravity, Mylar G) and is kept as words. The oxygen numbers are differences between limits, not an atmosphere.

OF2012.test1env.text: Test 1 is a pass/fail upward flame propagation test conducted in the most severe flaming combustion environment (oxygen concentration, pressure) expected in the spacecraft, currently 30% oxygen at 10.2 psia.
OF2012.test1env.quote: The method is a pass/fail upward flame propagation test conducted in the most severe flaming combustion environment (oxygen concentration, pressure) expected in the spacecraft

OF2012.uloi.text: 1g ULOI: the oxygen concentration at which a material passes the NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 burn length criterion approximately half the time. 1g MOC: the oxygen concentration where at least five samples passed and at least one sample failed at 1 percent more oxygen by volume.
OF2012.uloi.quote: ULOI is defined as the oxygen concentration at which a material passes the NASA STD 6001 Test 1 burn length criterion approximately half the time.

OF2012.normoxic.text: Keeping oxygen partial pressure constant while reducing total pressure increases the concentration of oxygen, which in turn leads to increased flammability of materials.
OF2012.normoxic.quote: partial pressure constant while reducing total pressure has the effect of increasing the concentration of oxygen which in turn leads to increased flammability of materials.

oxygen_pressure: Keeping oxygen partial pressure constant while reducing total pressure

SAE2008.uloi.text: 1g Upward Limiting Oxygen Index (ULOI) and 1g Maximum Oxygen Concentration (MOC) were greater than those in 0g by up to 4% oxygen mole fraction.

SAE2008.spread.text: Flame spread rate is correlated with flow velocity, oxygen concentration and pressure.

SAE2008.mocpressure.text: The White Sands Test 1 data show that the 1g MOCs depend mainly on oxygen concentration and generally only weakly on pressure; a few fuels, which appear to share halogen species, depend more strongly on pressure.

SAE2008.table1.text: Each 1g and 0g limit in Table 1 is printed together with its pressure (14.7 or 10.2 psia) and, for 0g, the flow speed (30 cm/s).
SAE2008.table1.tagging_note: Two pressures are written without saying which limit has which, and the flow speed is written for the 0g limits only; both are kept as words.

CP2003.det.particles.text: Microgravity detector performance differed from 1-g performance in the Comparative Soot Diagnostics experiment; the difference was attributed to larger smoke particles.
CP2003.det.particles.quote: This performance difference was attributed to the growth of larger smoke particles in 0-g because of the increased residence time in high smoke concentration regions (Ref. 5).

SAF.result.text: Saffire-I, 20 cm/s air flow, cotton-fiberglass fabric 40.6 x 94 cm: average spread rate 1.8 mm/s concurrent and 1.3 mm/s opposed.

SAF.starting_o2.text: The paper attributes the slightly faster spread of the 5-cm-wide sample to the slightly higher starting oxygen percentage, 22.1% (Saffire-II) against 21.7% (Saffire-I).
SAF.starting_o2.quote: This may be due to the slightly higher starting oxygen percentage (22.1% vs. 21.7%).
SAF.starting_o2.tagging_note: The two oxygen values belong to two flights; they are normalized as one range.

SAF.sensors.text: Oxygen concentration, carbon dioxide and pressure were recorded just upstream of the fuel in the flow duct.
SAF.sensors.quote: Oxygen concentration, carbon dioxide, and pressure were also recorded just upstream of the fuel in the flow duct.
SAF.sensors.tagging_note: States what was recorded and where; it reports no value.

SAME.sizes.text: Particle sizes ranged from 100 to 600 nm; zero-flow conditions produced particles on average double the size of those at the nominal 8.1 cm/s; particle sizes increase with aging.

flow: zero-flow conditions produced particles on average double the size of those at the nominal 8.1 cm/s

SAME.sizes.tagging_note: Two flow conditions are compared (zero flow and 8.1 cm/s); they are kept as words.

SAME.detector.text: The ISS smoke detector (light scattering, calibrated with 0.6 micrometre particles) showed reduced performance for Kapton and Teflon smoke.

SAME.keyparams.text: Parameters that the investigators name as governing the smoke properties.
SAME.keyparams.quote: the convective flow past the heated wire, the wire temperature, the aging time and the low-gravity condition.

FLEX.loi.text: Limiting Oxygen Index (LOI): the oxygen mole fraction below which a steady flame cannot exist for a given material and ambient condition. In total flooding, the goal of the agent is to reduce the oxygen concentration below the LOI.
FLEX.loi.quote: For fire safety, the goal of the agent in a total flooding application is to reduce the oxygen concentration below the LOI

FLEX.mec.text: Minimum Extinction Concentration (MEC): the minimum suppressant concentration above which a quasi-steady flame cannot exist. LOI = 0.209 (1 - MEC).

MST14.loi.text: LOI in oxygen/nitrogen: 0.12 for methanol and 0.15 for heptane; with carbon dioxide dispersed into air at 1 atm: about 0.14 and 0.17.

pressure: with carbon dioxide dispersed into air at 1 atm

MST14.loi.tagging_note: '1 atm' is written for the carbon-dioxide values only and is kept as words. The LOI numbers are results, written as fractions.

TP216046.disruptive.text: In the initial FLEX tests, which focused on ambient conditions with higher oxygen mole fractions, the science team noticed as testing progressed a propensity for the droplets to burn disruptively and not exhibit flame extinction at a finite-sized droplet diameter; the latter half of the test matrix focused on lower oxygen mole fractions, where both diffusive and radiative extinction occurred (Table IV for methanol, Table V for heptane).
TP216046.disruptive.quote: As testing progressed, however, the science team noticed a propensity for the droplets to burn disruptively and not exhibit flame extinction (at a finite-sized droplet diameter).

TP216046.diffusive_contam.text: The report states that the diffusive extinction droplet diameters (smaller diameters) of methanol were minimally influenced by the presence of the fuel needle contaminant, and that radiative extinction droplet diameters (larger diameters) were not influenced by it.
TP216046.diffusive_contam.quote: The diffusive extinction droplet diameters (smaller diameters) for methanol (where there is no disruption) were minimally influenced by the presence of the contaminant.

RG.test1.text: Test 1 is not conservative: materials can burn at lower oxygen levels in microgravity than on Earth.

RG.ignite.quote: Materials are easier to ignite in low gravity because of reduced natural convective cooling from the fuel surface.

RG.map.text: Flammability map of a material: sensitivity to ventilation flow, oxygen concentration and possibly pressure; the limiting oxygen concentration is the worst case over these.
RG.map.quote: The goal is to obtain the microgravity flammability map for select materials to provide information on the sensitivity of the material’s flammability to ventilation flow, ambient oxygen concentration and possibly pressure, to find the fundamental limiting oxygen concentration in microgravity.

RG.ignition.text: Ignition is measured as a time to ignition, as a function of environmental conditions, with an externally applied heat flux.
RG.ignition.quote: Time to ignition and the time between introduction of suppression agent and extinction are measured as a function of environmental conditions.

SAF456.limits_exceeded.text: Preliminary result: the paper states that the allowable CO2 level, which it gives as a 1-hour average CO2 partial pressure of no more than 3 mm Hg, was exceeded by both PMMA tests on Saffire VI (CO2 partial pressure increases of 3.51 and 3.37 mmHg in Table 2), and that the carbon monoxide levels were well above the 24-hour SMAC of 100 ppm and quite close to the 1-hour SMAC of 425 ppm (CO increases of 308 and 320 ppm in Table 2).
SAF456.limits_exceeded.quote: the allowable CO2 level was exceeded by both of the PMMA tests on Saffire VI.
SAF456.limits_exceeded.tagging_note: Two samples (VI-3, VI-4) with different conditions; no condition is normalized.
SAF456.limits_exceeded.relation: related NASA experiment, not a PSI investigation of this catalogue

SAF456.alarm.text: Preliminary result: in Saffire VI-3 (two-sided PMMA; 54.6 kPa and 30.3 mol % oxygen in Table 1), with 1 mg/m3 selected as a relatively tight alarm threshold, the far-field detector reached that threshold at 981 seconds; the paper states that by this point much of the hazardous gas release had occurred. The duct flow was changed from 20 cm/s to 5 cm/s at 1120 s.
SAF456.alarm.quote: Selecting 1 mg/m3 as a relatively tight alarm threshold, the FFD detector reached that threshold at 981 seconds.

flow: changed from 20 cm/s to 5 cm/s at 1120 s

SAF456.alarm.relation: related NASA experiment, not a PSI investigation of this catalogue

SAF456.hazard.text: Preliminary result: the paper concludes, from fires of 1.5 to 3.2 kW in unmanned spacecraft with free air volumes of 17 to 19 cubic meters, that the temperature increased significantly only very near the fire, that carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide rose significantly, and that the human hazard from a fire in a spacecraft is very similar to terrestrial fires, where the heat is not the principal hazard and the smoke and gaseous products are a much greater concern.
SAF456.hazard.quote: the heat from the fire is not the principal hazard and rather the smoke and gaseous products are a much greater concern
SAF456.hazard.tagging_note: Tagged D1 (gaseous products, CO, CO2) and D2 (smoke).
SAF456.hazard.relation: related NASA experiment, not a PSI investigation of this catalogue

SAF17S.flame_length_plateau.text: Saffire-I (40.6-cm-wide SIBAL cotton-fiberglass fabric, 20 cm/s flow, initial oxygen 21.7% by ISS reading): for the concurrent flame the length reached a plateau value of around 40 mm, while the opposed-flow flame was a bit shorter at 24 mm.

SAF17S.flame_length_plateau.tagging_note: A flame length plateau is tagged P3 (fire growth). The oxygen is the initial ISS reading.

SAF17S.narrow_sample_spread.text: At the same flow speed of 20 cm/s, the flame spread rate of the 5-cm-wide SIBAL fabric sample (Saffire-2) was marginally faster than that of the 40.6-cm-wide sample (Saffire-1): 2.1 compared to 1.8 mm/s; the slide attributes this partly to the slightly higher starting oxygen percentage (22.1% vs. 21.7%) and says the narrow sample might also have spread faster because of larger side entrainment effects.
SAF17S.narrow_sample_spread.quote: The flame spread rate for the 5-cm-wide sample is marginally faster compared to the spread rate for the 40.6-cm-wide sample
SAF17S.narrow_sample_spread.tagging_note: The two starting oxygen values of a comparison are normalized as a range, as for SAF.starting_o2.

SAF17S.saffire2_ignition.text: Saffire-2 ignition power for all samples except the thick PMMA: 80 W for 9.2 s, 16 W/cm per unit fuel width; the ignition energy and time for samples 2-1 through 2-7 were chosen to mimic the NASA 6001 Test 1 ignition, 736 J applied uniformly for 9.2 s.
SAF17S.saffire2_ignition.quote: chosen to mimic the NASA 6001 Test 1 ignition, 736 J applied uniformly for 9.2 s
SAF17S.saffire2_ignition.tagging_note: States the igniter, not an observation of ignition; tagged result as a reported test condition (rule 'kind').

SAF17S.saffire2_thick_pmma_ignition.text: Saffire-2 ignition power for the thick PMMA samples: 97 W for 30 s, 19.5 W/cm per unit fuel width; samples 2-8 and 2-9 had slightly more powerful igniters (97 W instead of 80 W) and were left on longer (30 s instead of 9.2 s) to assure ignition of these thick fuels.
SAF17S.saffire2_thick_pmma_ignition.quote: Samples 2-8 and 2-9 had slightly more powerful igniters (97 W instead of 80 W)
SAF17S.saffire2_thick_pmma_ignition.tagging_note: States the igniter, a reported test condition.

SAF17S.saffire1_ignition.text: Saffire-1 ignition power (40.6-cm-wide SIBAL fabric): 165 W for 8 s, 4.1 W/cm per unit fuel width.

SAF17S.saffire1_ignition.tagging_note: States the igniter, a reported test condition.

SAF17S.silicone_no_spread.text: None of the Saffire-2 silicone samples (sheets 0.27, 0.61, 1.03 and 0.37 mm thick, samples 2-1 to 2-4) burned: when the igniter was powered off a tiny gas phase flame remained but did not spread and quickly extinguished; the slide notes that even the thin sample had been entirely consumed in normal gravity.

SAF17S.silicone_no_spread.tagging_note: Tagged P1 (flammability of a material) and P3 (no flame spread). 'normal gravity' is written for the comparison only.

SAF45.table2_flame_size#II-6.quote: The steady state flame lengths are summarized in Table 2.

SAF45.v3_pmma_flame_length.text: Preliminary result: in Saffire V-3, a one-sided PMMA sample (0.5 cm thick, 18 cm long) in concurrent air flow of 20 cm/s at 71.3 kPa, the flame (in 25.4% oxygen) grew to 11 cm after 450 seconds; the paper states that in these cases the flame length reached an upper limit, contrary to similar 1-g tests that did not reach a steady length.
SAF45.v3_pmma_flame_length.quote: In Saffire V-3, the one-sided PMMA sample flame (in 25.4% oxygen) grew to 11 cm after 450 seconds.
SAF45.v3_pmma_flame_length.tagging_note: '1-g' is written for the comparison tests only and is kept as words; the item states no gravity level for V-3.
SAF45.v3_pmma_flame_length.relation: related NASA experiment, not a PSI investigation of this catalogue

SAF45.iv2_v3_no_spread#IV-2.text: Preliminary result: in the two concurrent PMMA samples of Saffire IV and V (IV-2: two-sided, 1 cm thick, at 100.0 kPa and 22.0 mol % oxygen; V-3: one-sided, 0.5 cm thick, at 71.3 kPa and 25.4 mol % oxygen; air flow 20 cm/s), the flames did not spread appreciably and remained fixed at the leading edge of the sample, advancing through surface regression only.
SAF45.iv2_v3_no_spread#IV-2.quote: Both concurrent samples (IV-2 and V-3) did not spread appreciably and instead remained fixed at the leading edge of the sample
SAF45.iv2_v3_no_spread#IV-2.relation: related NASA experiment, not a PSI investigation of this catalogue

THOMSEN19.conditions.text: Saffire-II sample 9 (10 mm PMMA slab) was burned in air at 200 mm/s flow and atmospheric pressure (100 kPa in the abstract). No oxygen percentage is given for the flight sample.
THOMSEN19.conditions.quote: The PMMA sample was burned in air with a 200 mm/s flow and atmospheric pressure.
THOMSEN19.conditions.tagging_note: The flow is written as 200 mm/s; the normalized 20 cm/s is the item's own values key flow_cms. No oxygen percentage is written ('in air').

SAMEEIRD.csd.text: The sentences of the PSI-102 'approach' field about an igniter, thermophoretic soot samplers, weighing the remains of the samples and flight mass loss rates stand in this document in section 1.2.2, under the heading '1.2 Background: CSD experiment design and results'.
SAMEEIRD.csd.quote: The remains of the samples were weighed to determine their mass loss. The digital data was transcribed from the video record and analyzed to determine the response of the detectors. Once the flight mass loss rates were determined, 1-g operation conditions to produce the same loss were determined.

SAMEFSR.results.text: Table 1 'Results of SAME flight tests' gives, for Kapton, lamp wick, silicone and Teflon, unaged and aged: geometric mean diameter, arithmetic mean diameter, diameter of average mass (nm) and geometric standard deviation.
SAMEFSR.results.quote: Results from the moment instruments for baseline runs (no aging) and 720 second aging runs are summarized in Table 1.
SAMEFSR.results.tagging_note: Says where the results are and for which materials; the item holds no value.

SAMEFSR.massloss.text: For the 2007 flight, the mass loss analysis of the returned samples is reported as started but not completed (2008 conference paper reprinted in the report). No table of measured SAME-1 mass losses was found in the report.
SAMEFSR.massloss.quote: At this time the samples and TEM grids have been received back from the ISS; TEM and mass loss analyses have been initiated but not completed.

SAMER.rtr0.limit.text: The same Rt/R0 does not mean the same sample temperature: the derived heating temperatures differed by up to 30 degrees Celsius at equal Rt/R0.
SAMER.rtr0.limit.quote: it is surprising that for the same Rt/R0, the actual heating temperature difference can be as large as 30 degrees Celsius.

SAMER.massloss.text: The mass loss of each SAME-R sample was measured after the flight by weighing (Appendix C lists preflight average, postflight average and mass loss in mg by sample and test number). These values are not in the PSI-101 experimental table.
SAMER.massloss.quote: After entire SAMER tests were completed, the six carousels, all tested samples and the six thermal precipitators were shipped to the GRC for measuring sample weight losses and TEM grid analysis.
SAMER.massloss.tagging_note: Says that the mass loss was measured and where it is listed; the item holds no value.

TM217036.signatures.text: Fire signatures defined as the gaseous species and particulate properties produced by a fire.
TM217036.signatures.quote: However, advanced sensors require knowledge of the fire signatures, i.e., the gaseous species and particulate properties produced by a fire that provide the quickest and most reliable detection.

CP2004.flam.fist.text: Quantities named for ranking the hazard of materials in the Forced Ignition and Spread Test: time to ignition, fire spread rate, material properties, critical heat flux.
CP2004.flam.fist.quote: Develop a flammability test method to rank the hazards of materials used on spacecraft using time to ignition, fire spread rate, material properties, critical heat flux

WP21.emission.text: Smoke emission factor: mass of smoke component per mass of fuel burned.
WP21.emission.quote: smoke emission factors (i.e., mass of smoke component per mass fuel burned)

WP21.same.text: The white paper's summary of the SAME detector result.
WP21.same.quote: the ISS detector failed to alarm for Kapton smoke in half of the tests and for Teflon smoke in two-thirds of the tests

ICES15.first.text: The investigators call the data the first extensive data on the stoichiometry and toxicity of combustion products in microgravity.
ICES15.first.quote: the data reported here is the first extensive data on the stoichiometry and toxicity of combustion products in microgravity

ICES15.co_per_co2.text: In the BASS-II PMMA tests (microgravity combustion tests in the glovebox), the concurrent rods produced on average 550 ppm of CO for every 1% of CO2, the opposed thick slabs on average 370 ppm of CO for every 1% of CO2, and the opposed rods had a very non-linear response.
ICES15.co_per_co2.quote: The concurrent rods produced on average 550 ppm of CO for every 1% of CO2.

ICES15.stoich.text: The BASS-II data, taken over a wide range of initial oxygen concentrations, forced opposed or concurrent flow velocities and sample geometries, agree very well with the PMMA stoichiometric ratio (6O2 : 5 CO2), which the paper takes to indicate that the vast majority of the oxygen consumed went into carbon dioxide; one outlier at 2.8% CO2 had the CO sensor over-ranged (> 1000 ppm).
ICES15.stoich.quote: the vast majority of the oxygen consumed did indeed go into carbon dioxide

oxygen: a wide range of initial oxygen concentrations

ICES15.coratio_flue.text: The paper plots the CO/CO2 ratio of the BASS-II tests against the initial oxygen concentration and states that for efficiently burned flue gases the ratio is on the order of 0.002, that most of the BASS-II data are an order of magnitude above that, and that this indicates microgravity flames are not very efficient.
ICES15.coratio_flue.quote: For efficiently burned flue gasses (boilers, furnaces, etc.), this ratio is on the order of 0.002.

ICES15.hrr.text: Computed by the authors, not a measurement: using Huggett's oxygen consumption calorimetry (13.1 kJ/g O2) and the burn time of each test, the paper estimates the BASS-II heat release rate to be typically well below 100 W, increasing with ambient oxygen; one long opposed thick slab test released close to 100 W and a brief concurrent rod test almost 110 W.
ICES15.hrr.quote: we estimate the heat release rate to be typically well below 100 W
ICES15.hrr.tagging_note: A heat release estimate names no gas, smoke, spread, ignition or extinction; tagged general (the collecting agent proposed D1).

ICES15.phi.text: Computed by the authors, not a measurement: from the mass loss and oxygen consumption of 19 usable returned samples, the paper estimates the BASS-II global equivalence ratio to be 1.3 on average (fuel rich), and states that the flames were under-ventilated, with some fuel ending up as soot, some as CO and some as unburned hydrocarbons.
ICES15.phi.quote: the global equivalence ratio for the tests is estimated to be 1.3 on average, which indicates the flames were burning fuel rich

ICES15.us_lab_co.text: Computed by the authors, not a measurement: the paper estimates that the combustion products of a fire of the scale of a BASS-II test, diluted within the US Lab (106 m3 pressurized volume), would give CO levels of only 1.5 ppm, and compares this with SMAC values of 10 ppm for long term exposure and 55 ppm for 1 hour.
ICES15.us_lab_co.quote: even within just the US Lab (106 m3 pressurized volume), the CO levels in the lab would only be 1.5 ppm

BASS2TM.igndelay.text: Ignition delay as defined and reported by the investigators for the PMMA rod tests, plotted against the initial oxygen concentration.
BASS2TM.igndelay.quote: The ignition delay (tign) in each test was defined as the time from when the igniter was first turned on to the last time the igniter was turned off and a stable flame persisted.

BASS2TM.coratio.text: The investigators present the CO/CO2 ratio as a measure of completeness of combustion, of interest to the combustion community.
BASS2TM.coratio.quote: Of interest to the combustion community is the ratio of CO to CO2, a measure of completeness of combustion

BASS2SUM.pressure_range.text: In the BASS-II opposed-flow tests on thin PMMA sheets reported in section 2.3, the total pressure was monitored and varied from 99.2 to 99.5 kPa.
BASS2SUM.pressure_range.quote: The total pressure is also monitored, which varied from 99.2 to 99.5 kPa in the tests reported.

BASS2SUM.sibal_1atm.text: For the BASS-II concurrent-flow tests on SIBAL composite fabric the ambient pressure is stated as 1 atm.

BASS2SUM.vitiation.text: BASS-II used gaseous nitrogen available on the ISS to vitiate the atmosphere in the Microgravity Science Glovebox from standard ISS air down to the low oxygen flammability limits.
BASS2SUM.vitiation.quote: BASS–II utilized the gaseous nitrogen (GN2) available on International Space Station (ISS) to vitiate the atmosphere in the Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) from standard ISS “air” down to the low O2 flammability limits.

oxygen: from standard ISS air down to the low oxygen flammability limits

BASS2TM.table5_1#M1.quote: A total of 20 PMMA flat samples were burnt during the BASS–II experimentation (Table 5.1). The sample thickness varied from 1 to 5 mm thick.

BASS2TM.table5_1#M20.text: BASS-II opposed-flow tests on flat PMMA samples, Table 5.1: for each of the 20 tests the thickness (1 to 5 mm), width, one or two sides burning, opposed-flow velocity, flame spread rate, burn time and initial and final O2 (vol%) as printed; where a test lists several velocities, the spread rates are printed in the same order.
BASS2TM.table5_1#M20.quote: A total of 20 PMMA flat samples were burnt during the BASS–II experimentation (Table 5.1). The sample thickness varied from 1 to 5 mm thick.

BASS2TM.thin_pmma_spread_vs_1g.text: In the BASS-II opposed-flow tests on 100-µm-thick PMMA sheet, the highest spread rate in microgravity was 2.2 mm/s, with the opposing flow velocity varied from about 40 cm/s to about 1 cm/s; the average spread rate of the normal-gravity (downward) experiments, run at 101 kPa and 21 percent O2, was 2.0 mm/s. The report states the two are about the same.
BASS2TM.thin_pmma_spread_vs_1g.quote: The highest spread rate in the microgravity environment, 2.2 mm/s, is about the same as the downward spread rate.

oxygen_pressure: run at 101 kPa and 21 percent O2

BASS2TM.thin_pmma_spread_vs_1g.tagging_note: The 101 kPa and 21 percent O2 are written for the normal-gravity part of the comparison only and are kept as words.

BASS2TM.rod_ignition_delay.text: In the BASS-II tests on PMMA rods ignited with a hot wire, ignition generally occurred at a forced flow of 5 cm/s; at higher O2 concentrations ignition occurred within approximately 40 s, below an initial O2 concentration of 16 percent the ignition delay time increased significantly, and larger rods took longer to ignite, especially at lower O2 concentrations (up to 230 s).
BASS2TM.rod_ignition_delay.quote: At higher O2 concentrations, ignition occurred within approximately 40 s. Below an initial O2 concentration of 16 percent, the ignition delay time increased significantly.
BASS2TM.rod_ignition_delay.tagging_note: The O2 numbers (16 percent, 'higher', 'lower') describe where the delay changed; they are results, not the atmosphere of one test, and are not normalized.

BASS2TM.rod_ignition_limit.text: In the BASS-II PMMA rod tests, below an initial O2 concentration of about 14.5 percent a sustained ignition could not be achieved, although flames were observed while the igniter was on; at very low O2, ignition times up to 500 s did not give a sustained flame with the initial flow varied from 2 to 10 cm/s. Flames ignited at a higher O2 survived to final O2 concentrations as low as 13.6 percent.
BASS2TM.rod_ignition_limit.quote: Below an initial O2 concentration of ~14.5 percent O2, a sustained ignition could not be achieved even though flames were observed when the igniter was on
BASS2TM.rod_ignition_limit.tagging_note: The O2 numbers are reported limits and final readings, not the atmosphere of a test, and are not normalized. Tagged P2 (ignition); the item also states an oxygen limit for ignition.

BASS2TM.rod_quench_flame_aspect.text: In the BASS-II PMMA rod quenching test at the lowest O2 (rod radius 0.476 cm), with the O2 going from an initial setting of 14.8 percent to a final reading of 13.6 percent (by volume) and the flow decreased in steps, the rod regression reached an apparently steady-state rate of 0.0385 mm/s and the flame aspect ratio (L/W) decreased incrementally to 0.5 at extinction.
BASS2TM.rod_quench_flame_aspect.quote: The aspect ratio (L/W) decreases incrementally to 0.5 at extinction, indicating a hemispherical flame at the quenching limit.
BASS2TM.rod_quench_flame_aspect.tagging_note: Tagged S1 by the words 'quenching' and 'extinction'; the collecting agent proposed P3.

BASS2TM.extvel.text: In BASS-II tests on thin PMMA sheets with the opposed flow reduced until the flame went out, the extinction velocities were about 1 cm/s for 100, 200 and 300 µm and about 1.5 cm/s for 400 µm thickness; the report notes significant uncertainties in these values because the flow calibration at such low velocity has high error bars.
BASS2TM.extvel.quote: the extinction velocities are found to be about 1 cm/s for 100, 200, and 300 μm and about 1.5 cm/s for 400 μm.

flow: opposed flow reduced until the flame went out

BASS2TM.extvel_o2.text: At a lower O2 level of about 16 percent, the BASS-II extinction velocities over thin PMMA were about 2.6 cm/s for 100 µm (sample 20 mm wide) and about 4 cm/s for 200 µm (sample 10 mm wide); the report states that the extinction velocity significantly increases as the O2 level decreases, and that the data at the lower O2 level are few.
BASS2TM.extvel_o2.quote: Tests were also conducted at a lower O2 level of about 16 percent for two different thicknesses and the extinction velocities were found to be about 2.6 cm/s for 100 μm and about 4 cm/s for 200 μm.

BASS2TM.extvel_model.text: Computed by the authors, not a measurement: in the investigators' computational model of opposed-flow flame spread over 100-µm-thick PMMA sheet, the extinction velocity is 3.5 cm/s at 16 percent O2 as opposed to 1.5 cm/s at 21 percent O2; the computations at 21 percent use a 21/79 O2/N2 mixture at 1 atm.
BASS2TM.extvel_model.quote: The extinction velocity is found to be 3.5 cm/s as opposed to 1.5 cm/s at 21 percent O2.

oxygen: at 16 percent O2 as opposed to 1.5 cm/s at 21 percent O2

BASS2TM.extvel_model.tagging_note: Two oxygen levels are compared; the 1 atm is written for the 21 percent computations only. Both are kept as words.

BASS2TM.rod_spread_limit.text: In the BASS-II opposed-flow tests on black PMMA rods (6.35, 9.525 and 12.7 mm diameter), flame spread was observed at O2 concentrations as low as 17.5 percent in microgravity, while in normal gravity flame spread was not observed below 19 percent; the report attributes this probably to the lower opposed-flow velocity in the microgravity tests.
BASS2TM.rod_spread_limit.quote: While in microgravity, flame spread was observed at O2 concentrations as low as 17.5 percent, in normal gravity, flame spread was not observed below 19 percent.
BASS2TM.rod_spread_limit.tagging_note: The O2 numbers are the lowest O2 with flame spread, results and not the atmosphere of one test. Tagged P1 (an oxygen threshold) and P3 (flame spread); the collecting agent proposed S1.

BASS2TM.rod_min_o2.text: For the BASS-II concurrent-flow PMMA rod tests, the report gives the minimum O2 concentration of the flammability boundary as 13.5 percent O2 at a stretch rate a of 8 to 12 s-1, lower than the upward flame spread limit of 15.4 percent O2 observed in normal gravity with an additional 4-cm/s forced flow.
BASS2TM.rod_min_o2.quote: The minimum O2 concentration of 13.5 percent O2 at a of 8 to 12 s–1 is significantly lower than the observed upward flame spread limit of 15.4 percent O2
BASS2TM.rod_min_o2.tagging_note: The O2 numbers are reported limits, not the atmosphere of a test. 'normal gravity' and the 4-cm/s flow are written for the comparison limit only. Tagged P1 as ICES19.limits; the collecting agent proposed S1.

BASS2TM.blowoff.text: The report concludes for the BASS-II PMMA rod tests that blowoff extinction limits from the ISS experiments agree well with the limits of 5.18-s drop tests in the Zero Gravity Research Facility.
BASS2TM.blowoff.quote: Blowoff extinction limits from the ISS experiments agree well with Zero Gravity Research Facility 5.18-s drop test limits.

CFI14.o2series#R377.text: For FLEX n-decane droplets in microgravity at 0.5 atm pressure (R377: 4.03 mm, 21% O2; R374: 3.79 mm, 25% O2; R379: 3.86 mm, 17% O2; R383: 3.14 mm, 14% O2), the authors summarize that reducing the ambient oxygen concentration leads to earlier hot and cool flame extinctions: the R377 flame extinguished abruptly at around 14.6 seconds, R379 had radiative extinction at 7 seconds, and the R374 droplet micro-exploded 26 seconds after ignition.

CFI14.helium.text: For FLEX n-octane droplets in microgravity at 1 atm and an oxygen mole fraction held at 0.21, with helium replacing nitrogen at 0, 15, 50 and 75% by volume (tests R298, R694, R698, R707), the burning rate constants of the two stages rose with helium (0.48 and 0.38, 0.54 and 0.43, 0.63 and 0.53 mm2/s for the first three), the burning times were considerably shortened, cool flame extinction in R298 occurred at 30.5 seconds, and at 75% helium (R707, D0 2.49 mm) first stage burning was almost eliminated.

THOMSEN18.care.text: Care should be taken interpreting and applying results obtained at reduced pressure, because eventually low pressure will affect the chemical kinetics of the process.
THOMSEN18.care.quote: Thus, care should be taken interpreting and applying these results, particularly because eventually low pressure will affect the chemical kinetics of the process.

NIEHAUS15.expected.text: Silicone was chosen for Saffire-II because its flammability limit is close to the expected test atmosphere (air; 21% O2, 1 atm).
NIEHAUS15.expected.quote: Silicone was chosen because its flammability limit is close to the expected test atmosphere (air; 21% O2, 1 atm)
NIEHAUS15.expected.tagging_note: The atmosphere is the one expected in 2015, before the flights ('expected test atmosphere'); kind is set to result although the sentence states an expectation and a reason for choosing the material.

URBAN14.loc.text: Tests with Nomex HT90-40 found the limiting oxygen concentration for flame spread as a function of ambient pressure in a quiescent environment; the authors report a strong dependence on pressure.
URBAN14.loc.quote: The strong dependence on pressure suggests either kinetic effects or flow effects.

pressure: as a function of ambient pressure

URBAN14.normoxic.text: The poster states that at constant oxygen partial pressure, such as in normoxic equivalent atmospheres, the ambient pressure can decide whether a fire resistant material becomes flammable.
URBAN14.normoxic.quote: oxygen partial pressure, such as in normoxic equivalent atmospheres, it is possible that a fire resistant material can become flammable depending on the ambient pressure.

oxygen_pressure: constant oxygen partial pressure, such as in normoxic equivalent atmospheres

G125.scope.text: Per the public scope text, the method measures the threshold-limit conditions for combustion of materials in oxidant gases, for set values of pressure, temperature, flow, fire-propagation direction and system geometry.

G125.conditions.text: The public page cautions that fire-limit results may not hold for conditions that differ from those of the test, and that limits measured under one set of conditions need not be the lowest thresholds for combustion.

ZHAO15.quench_speed.text: In BASS and BASS-II tests on thin cotton-fiberglass (SIBAL) fabric in concurrent, purely forced flow in microgravity, at ambient O2 molar fractions of 16% to 21% and 1 atm, low-speed flame quenching extinction limits were found by decreasing the flow during some tests: the quenching speeds were between 1 and 5 cm/s, higher in lower oxygen.
ZHAO15.quench_speed.quote: The quenching speeds were found to be between 1 and 5 cm/s with higher speed in lower oxygen atmosphere.
ZHAO15.quench_speed.tagging_note: Tagged S1 by the words 'quenching extinction limits'; the collecting agent proposed P3.

ICES20407.optimal_baffle.text: In ISS tests in microgravity of concurrent, purely forced flow flame spread over thin SIBAL cotton-fiberglass fabric between two parallel baffles, with the glovebox at the ISS ambient values of 1.0 atm and ~22% O2, at an imposed flow of 7 cm/s the flame length first increased and then decreased as the inter-baffle distance D was reduced from no baffles (equivalent to D = 7.6 cm) to D = 2.0 cm; the maximum flame length occurred at around D = 4.0 cm, where the spread rate also reached its maximum for all baffle types.
ICES20407.optimal_baffle.quote: The maximum flame length occurs at around D = 4.0 cm.
ICES20407.optimal_baffle.tagging_note: '~22%' is normalized as 22; the paper gives a daily variation of 21.3% to 22.9% in the glovebox.
ICES20407.optimal_baffle.relation: related NASA experiment, not a PSI investigation of this catalogue

ICES20407.no_ignition_D1.text: In ISS tests in microgravity of concurrent, purely forced flow flame spread over thin SIBAL cotton-fiberglass fabric between two parallel baffles, with the glovebox at the ISS ambient values of 1.0 atm and ~22% O2 (imposed flows of 5 to 28 cm/s), ignition was not achieved for any baffle type at an inter-baffle distance of D = 1.0 cm.
ICES20407.no_ignition_D1.quote: At D = 1.0 cm, ignition was not achieved for any baffle types.
ICES20407.no_ignition_D1.tagging_note: '~22%' is normalized as 22; the paper gives a daily variation of 21.3% to 22.9% in the glovebox.
ICES20407.no_ignition_D1.relation: related NASA experiment, not a PSI investigation of this catalogue

ICES20407.steady_vs_growing.text: In ISS tests in microgravity of concurrent, purely forced flow flame spread over thin SIBAL cotton-fiberglass fabric between two parallel baffles, with the glovebox at the ISS ambient values of 1.0 atm and ~22% O2, when the imposed flow velocity was less than 15 cm/s steady state flame spread was observed for most of the tests; above 15 cm/s the flame continually grew and did not reach a steady state, except when the inter-baffle distance was small (< 3 cm). The paper notes that this observation might be specific to the tested sample length.
ICES20407.steady_vs_growing.quote: the flame continually grows and does not reach a steady state except when the inter-baffle distance is small (< 3 cm)
ICES20407.steady_vs_growing.tagging_note: '~22%' is normalized as 22; the paper gives a daily variation of 21.3% to 22.9% in the glovebox.
ICES20407.steady_vs_growing.relation: related NASA experiment, not a PSI investigation of this catalogue

LUCI25.sibal_spread.text: In the Lunar Combustion Investigation (LUCI) on a spinning New Shepard sounding rocket, where centrifugal acceleration gave simulated Lunar gravity and the samples burned in air at normal pressure, a 5-cm-wide SIBAL cotton-fiberglass fabric burning downward had a flame base spread rate of .92 mm/s and a flame tip spread rate of 1.1 mm/s; the spread rates of char front, flame base and flame tip were all linear (steady state spread).
LUCI25.sibal_spread.tagging_note: The gravity is simulated by centrifugal acceleration (11 RPM, effective radius 1.22 m, slide 12); the slides read print no g value. 'air at normal pressure' has no number and is kept as words.
LUCI25.sibal_spread.relation: related NASA experiment, not a PSI investigation of this catalogue

LUCI25.pmma_rod_spread.text: In the Lunar Combustion Investigation (LUCI) on a spinning New Shepard sounding rocket, where centrifugal acceleration gave simulated Lunar gravity and the samples burned in air at normal pressure, a 4-mm-diameter PMMA rod burning upward had an approximately linear flame tip spread, with a flame spread rate of 1.5 mm/s; the flame base spread rate was not constant and steady spread was not achieved (total base spread of ~6cm until extinction), and the chamber O2 decreased from 20% to 14.3%.
LUCI25.pmma_rod_spread.tagging_note: The gravity is simulated by centrifugal acceleration (11 RPM, effective radius 1.22 m, slide 12); the slides read print no g value. 'air at normal pressure' has no number and is kept as words.
LUCI25.pmma_rod_spread.relation: related NASA experiment, not a PSI investigation of this catalogue

MIST13.sim_ignition_0g_1g.text: Numerical simulation, not a measurement: in the MIST project's model of a PMMA sample under an external radiant heat flux of 16 kW/m2, with ambient pressure 100 kPa, oxygen concentration 21% and air flow velocity 0.4 m/s, ignition occurred significantly earlier at 0-g than at 1-g conditions (596 s compared to 774 s).
MIST13.sim_ignition_0g_1g.quote: ignition occurs significantly earlier at 0-g than at 1-g conditions (596 s compared to 774 s)
MIST13.sim_ignition_0g_1g.tagging_note: Conditions of a simulated case, not of a test.
MIST13.sim_ignition_0g_1g.relation: numerical simulation of a NASA-funded project, not a PSI investigation of this catalogue

NCM13.loi#0.7 atm.text: In FLEX tests in microgravity of methanol droplets burning in oxygen-nitrogen-carbon dioxide and oxygen-nitrogen-helium mixtures at 0.7 and 1 atmospheric pressures, the experiments show a limiting oxygen index for methanol in these diluent gases of around 12% to 13% oxygen by volume.
NCM13.loi#0.7 atm.quote: the limiting oxygen index for methanol in these diluent gases is around 12% to 13% oxygen by volume.
NCM13.loi#0.7 atm.tagging_note: One entry for each of the two pressures written; the LOI is a result and is not normalized. Tagged P1; the collecting agent proposed S1.

NCM13.loi#1 atm.text: In FLEX tests in microgravity of methanol droplets burning in oxygen-nitrogen-carbon dioxide and oxygen-nitrogen-helium mixtures at 0.7 and 1 atmospheric pressures, the experiments show a limiting oxygen index for methanol in these diluent gases of around 12% to 13% oxygen by volume.
NCM13.loi#1 atm.quote: the limiting oxygen index for methanol in these diluent gases is around 12% to 13% oxygen by volume.
NCM13.loi#1 atm.tagging_note: One entry for each of the two pressures written; the LOI is a result and is not normalized.

NCM13.radiative.text: In the FLEX methanol droplet tests in microgravity, radiative extinction was generally observed for larger droplets at lower oxygen concentrations, when the flame is large in size and lies farther away from the droplet surface; flame extinctions in both modes (diffusive and radiative) were observed.
NCM13.radiative.quote: this process is generally observed for larger droplets at lower oxygen concentrations when the flame is large in size

NCM13.de_runs.text: FLEX methanol droplets in microgravity burning at 0.7 atm in 21% O2 with 30% CO2 (run 110, initial diameter 2.83 mm) and with 30% He (run 263, initial diameter 2.67 mm), the remaining diluent being nitrogen in both cases, had extinction diameters of 1.57 mm and 1.42 mm, respectively.
NCM13.de_runs.quote: The extinction diameters De for run #110 and #263 were 1.57 mm and 1.42 mm, respectively.

NCM13.de_air.text: A FLEX methanol droplet in microgravity of 2.75 mm initial diameter, burning in air at one atmospheric pressure (1 atm in the Figure 2 caption), went out at a droplet diameter of 1.10 mm, the extinction diameter (run 204).
NCM13.de_air.quote: which occurs at a droplet diameter of 1.10 mm, called the extinction diameter De
NCM13.de_air.tagging_note: The paper prints 20% and 21% O2 for this run; no oxygen is normalized.

ASGSR20.xenon.text: The slides conclude, for normal-alkane droplets burning in microgravity, that xenon decreases burning rates substantially but can sustain cool flames at much lower oxygen concentrations than helium; no value is printed on the conclusions slide.
ASGSR20.xenon.quote: Xenon decreases burning rates substantially, but can sustain cool flames at much lower oxygen concentrations compared to helium.
ASGSR20.xenon.tagging_note: Tagged P1 (the oxygen at which a flame is sustained); the collecting agent proposed S1. A qualitative statement.

MIST03.flight.text: Preliminary result: in 32 tests in microgravity of the Water-Mist Fire Suppression Experiment on the STS-107 Space Shuttle mission (propane-air mixtures at stoichiometries of 0.6, 0.7, 1.0 and 1.3; water mass fractions from 0 up to 0.40; mean droplet sizes of 20 and 30 µm), the leanest propane-air flames showed progressively lower burning velocities with increasing water loadings and decreasing droplet size, with final extinction at the highest water concentrations; the paper prints no concentration at which extinction occurred.
MIST03.flight.quote: Preliminary results show that the leanest propane-air flames exhibit progressively lower burning velocities with increasing water loadings and decreasing droplet size (as predicted by the model) with final extinction at the highest water concentrations.

agent: water mass fractions from 0 up to 0.40

MIST03.flight.relation: related NASA experiment, not a PSI investigation of this catalogue

HAMINS03.n2.text: In counterflow methane-air non-premixed flames with nitrogen added to the fuel stream, measured in microgravity in the 2.2 s drop facility at NASA Glenn for strain rates of 7 s-1 through 50 s-1, the maximum nitrogen volume fraction in the fuel stream needed for extinction was 0.855 ± 0.016 at a strain rate of 15 s-1.
HAMINS03.n2.quote: The maximum nitrogen volume fraction in the fuel stream, Ca,ext, needed for extinction was found to be 0.855 ± 0.016 at a strain rate of 15 s-1
HAMINS03.n2.relation: related NASA experiment, not a PSI investigation of this catalogue

SAF45P.acid.text: In Saffire-IV and V, 0.59 g HCl (Saffire-IV) and 0.31 g HF (Saffire-V) were released in the cabin as tracer gases, and no acid gas was observed at the far-field diagnostics unit during either acid release event; HCl was observed during the Saffire-IV event 4 burn (SIBAL burn plus 0.59 g HCl release), and the slides give adsorption of the acid onto cabin surfaces as one possible explanation.
SAF45P.acid.quote: However, no acid gas was observed at the FFD during either acid release event!
SAF45P.acid.relation: related NASA experiment, not a PSI investigation of this catalogue

SAF45P.mixing.text: In the Saffire-IV and V tracer gas releases (CO2 measured at several locations in the Cygnus vehicle), the vehicle was approximately fully mixed at all locations by 400-500 elapsed seconds in Saffire-IV and by 300-400 elapsed seconds in Saffire-V; the slides attribute the difference to trash packing.
SAF45P.mixing.quote: Vehicle is ~fully mixed at all locations by 300-400 elapsed seconds
SAF45P.mixing.tagging_note: Transport of a tracer gas in the cabin; tagged D1 (gases).
SAF45P.mixing.relation: related NASA experiment, not a PSI investigation of this catalogue

SAF45P.particles.text: In all five Saffire-IV and V burn events the particle mass concentration at the far-field unit was dominated by submicron particles (PM1), which the slides call consistent with observations for flaming combustion; PMMA events produced higher concentrations of larger particles (dp > 4 µm) than cotton-containing samples, and the slides state that clogging of the flow unit outlet screen means the far-field measurements 'likely missed a significant fraction of larger particles'.
SAF45P.particles.quote: Particle mass concentration dominated by submicron particles (PM1) in all five burn events
SAF45P.particles.relation: related NASA experiment, not a PSI investigation of this catalogue

SAF45P.smokeeater.text: Little CO was removed by the smoke eater during the Saffire-IV and V burn events; the slides list catalyst fouling, bed packing integrity, CO concentrations at the far-field unit too low for substantial catalyst activity, and CO sensor problems as potential explanations, and the conclusions call it still under investigation.
SAF45P.smokeeater.quote: Little CO removed by the smoke eater during Saffire-IV and V burn events
SAF45P.smokeeater.relation: related NASA experiment, not a PSI investigation of this catalogue

SAME1R.detector.quote: The ISS detector showed a relatively weak signal for some Teflon runs doubtless a result of the particle size.

found.label: What NASA's experiments found
found.sentence: Quoted from the documents of the reference list. The grouping and the order are the team's, by a fixed rule on the conditions each statement states; they are not NASA's conclusions. A result is not carried from the condition where it was stated to another one.
found.printed_values_sentence: Printed values are the numbers of the item exactly as held in references.json, each with the column or quantity it was printed under. The team computes nothing with them.
found.all_questions_sentence: Results tagged for all questions are listed after the results tagged for this question, in the same groups and order.

process.label: Where this question sits in NASA's fire-safety process
process.sentence: Measures are quoted from NASA documents for the case they describe. The team recommends nothing.
process.team_reading: Team's reading (AI, not checked by a person): tests that record whether a solid material keeps burning at a recorded oxygen, pressure and flow relate to the evaluation of a material at its use environment and to the configuration evaluation.

found.all_questions_sentence: Results tagged for all questions are listed after the results tagged for this question, in the same groups and order.

The 17 tests counted for a need inside its oxygen and pressure ranges were recorded at 71.2 to 72.4 kPa, above 10.2 psi; the 9 tests inside the ranges recorded at 50.7 kPa are not counted for a need.

recorded.label: What PSI's tables record
recorded.sentence: Counts of tests in PSI's experimental tables as the team mapped them; the counts are the team's computation, not NASA's.

need.sentence: 133 tests in the scope of 'Flame spread and growth' (fuel_phase: solid) of investigations whose stated purpose names this subject (PSI-25; PSI-98; PSI-100) are in PSI's tables; 2 have an outcome of the need in a table cell (spread_rate_mm_s 0; burn_length_cm 0; burn_time_s 2); 2 are counted; 101 have a video tied to them by two labels.

unprocessed.label: In the archive, not in a table
unprocessed.sentence: A test is recorded, and a value this question needs is not in NASA's table. Listed here: the file groups that name these tests, how many files were opened, and what was read. A listed file group is not shown to hold the value.
unprocessed.lower_shelf_label: Not found in the files opened
unprocessed.lower_shelf_sentence: Not in a table, and no header accepted for it in any file opened so far. This is a statement about the files opened, not about the archive.

no_record.label: No record in PSI (listing of 14 November 2026)
no_record.sentence: No test at this condition is in PSI's per-test tables as the team mapped them, on one of the stated grounds, each printed with its source. The statement describes PSI's record on that date.

found.label: What NASA's experiments found
found.sentence: Quoted from the documents of the reference list. The grouping and the order are the team's, by a fixed rule on the conditions each statement states; they are not NASA's conclusions. A result is not carried from the condition where it was stated to another one.
found.printed_values_sentence: Printed values are the numbers of the item exactly as held in references.json, each with the column or quantity it was printed under. The team computes nothing with them.
found.all_questions_sentence: Results tagged for all questions are listed after the results tagged for this question, in the same groups and order.

process.label: Where this question sits in NASA's fire-safety process
process.sentence: Measures are quoted from NASA documents for the case they describe. The team recommends nothing.
process.team_reading: Team's reading (AI, not checked by a person): tests that record flame spread over a solid material relate to the configuration evaluation and to the measures that name propagation paths.

recorded.label: What PSI's tables record
recorded.sentence: Counts of tests in PSI's experimental tables as the team mapped them; the counts are the team's computation, not NASA's.

need.sentence: 133 tests in the scope of 'Flame spread and growth' (fuel_phase: solid) of investigations whose stated purpose names this subject (PSI-25; PSI-98; PSI-100) are in PSI's tables; 2 have an outcome of the need in a table cell (spread_rate_mm_s 0; burn_length_cm 0; burn_time_s 2); 2 are counted; 101 have a video tied to them by two labels.

unprocessed.label: In the archive, not in a table
unprocessed.sentence: A test is recorded, and a value this question needs is not in NASA's table. Listed here: the file groups that name these tests, how many files were opened, and what was read. A listed file group is not shown to hold the value.
unprocessed.lower_shelf_label: Not found in the files opened
unprocessed.lower_shelf_sentence: Not in a table, and no header accepted for it in any file opened so far. This is a statement about the files opened, not about the archive.

no_record.label: No record in PSI (listing of 14 November 2026)
no_record.sentence: No test at this condition is in PSI's per-test tables as the team mapped them, on one of the stated grounds, each printed with its source. The statement describes PSI's record on that date.

found.label: What NASA's experiments found
found.sentence: Quoted from the documents of the reference list. The grouping and the order are the team's, by a fixed rule on the conditions each statement states; they are not NASA's conclusions. A result is not carried from the condition where it was stated to another one.
found.printed_values_sentence: Printed values are the numbers of the item exactly as held in references.json, each with the column or quantity it was printed under. The team computes nothing with them.
found.all_questions_sentence: Results tagged for all questions are listed after the results tagged for this question, in the same groups and order.

found.printed_values_sentence: Printed values are the numbers of the item exactly as held in references.json, each with the column or quantity it was printed under. The team computes nothing with them.

recorded.label: What PSI's tables record
recorded.sentence: Counts of tests in PSI's experimental tables as the team mapped them; the counts are the team's computation, not NASA's.

need.sentence: 129 tests in the scope of 'Ignition' (fuel_phase: solid) of investigations whose stated purpose names this subject (PSI-25) are in PSI's tables; 0 have an outcome of the need in a table cell (hot_ignition 0); 0 are counted; 101 have a video tied to them by two labels.

unprocessed.label: In the archive, not in a table
unprocessed.sentence: A test is recorded, and a value this question needs is not in NASA's table. Listed here: the file groups that name these tests, how many files were opened, and what was read. A listed file group is not shown to hold the value.
unprocessed.lower_shelf_label: Not found in the files opened
unprocessed.lower_shelf_sentence: Not in a table, and no header accepted for it in any file opened so far. This is a statement about the files opened, not about the archive.

no_record.label: No record in PSI (listing of 14 November 2026)
no_record.sentence: No test at this condition is in PSI's per-test tables as the team mapped them, on one of the stated grounds, each printed with its source. The statement describes PSI's record on that date.

found.label: What NASA's experiments found
found.sentence: Quoted from the documents of the reference list. The grouping and the order are the team's, by a fixed rule on the conditions each statement states; they are not NASA's conclusions. A result is not carried from the condition where it was stated to another one.
found.printed_values_sentence: Printed values are the numbers of the item exactly as held in references.json, each with the column or quantity it was printed under. The team computes nothing with them.
found.all_questions_sentence: Results tagged for all questions are listed after the results tagged for this question, in the same groups and order.

unprocessed.label: In the archive, not in a table
